page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7se.large is a memory-optimized virtual instance belonging to the Enhanced family. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, it provisions 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core utilizing hyper-threading (2 threads per core) with dedicated CPU allocation. The instance features 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It operates under a KVM hypervisor, includes no bundled local storage, contains no GPU accelerators, and is provisioned with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Architectural features include AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI instruction set extensions.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable single-threaded execution constrained by low aggregate thread counts. In Geekbench, the server scores 1556.0 in single-core evaluations while scoring 1807.0 in multi-core metrics. A similar profile appears in stress-ng, registering 1874.59 in single-core and 1933.88 in multi-core operations. Single-threaded utility tasks perform steadily, reaching 27.81 GB/sec in gzip compression and 10.62 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Large-block memory transfers achieve 14.81 GB/sec for uncached reads and 13.68 GB/sec for writes. Database-oriented metrics show 1.95 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 1027.33 on PassMark database testing.

From an infrastructure cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU proportion permits deploying memory-heavy applications without over-provisioning compute cores. However, users should consider tradeoffs such as the baseline 1 Gbps network throughput and limited multi-threaded ceiling, which restrict intensive multi-user parallelism. The ecs.r7se.large is well-fitted for low-volume in-memory caching, development or staging database environments, lightweight ETL tasks, and microservices requiring a generous memory buffer relative to CPU demand.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7se.large is a memory-optimized cloud server within the Enhanced instance family, powered by a 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor on the x86_64 architecture. The virtual machine provisioned on KVM provides 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core with 2 threads, 16.0 GB of memory, a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmarks, the instance achieves average single-threaded performance, recording 1556.0 in single-core Geekbench and 27.81 GB/sec in gzip compression, but ranks in the lower percentiles for multi-core tests and uncached memory bandwidth due to its 2-vCPU configuration. Database workloads register 1.95 million Redis SET operations per second and 1027.33 in PassMark database operations. With an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, ecs.r7se.large is cost-efficient for smaller memory-intensive services such as modest Redis caches, lightweight relational databases, staging environments, and single-threaded data transformation jobs.
